text:
carmen: Heads-up: trying to push release v2.14.3 to prod but deploy-bot failed with permissions error. I think this started after the permission-boundary change yesterday. Anyone able to unlock a deploy or confirm?

deploy-bot: ERROR: assume-role failure for arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/deployer-prod — AccessDenied. Suggestion: check permission-boundary 'rbw-prod-boundary' denies sts:AssumeRole.

aj: ugh. saw that policy pushed in the afternoon. It tightened tag-based permissions. Might be denying cross-account assume roles for service accounts.

\cm: @carmen can you paste the exact error?

carmen: pasted above. also saw this in CI logs: `AccessDenied: User: arn:aws:sts::111111111111:assumed-role/ci-runner is not authorized to perform: sts:AssumeRole on resource deployer-prod`

maya: short term: we can add a temporary exception to the permission boundary to allow `sts:AssumeRole` for the deployer-prod role for the release window. Long term: need to move the deploy-bot into same account-role or use tag-based session tags.

simon: prefer minimal blast radius. proposal: create a short-lived cross-account role `deployer-releng-temp` with explicit allow for CI runner, MFA required, TTL 1h. Update deployer policy to trust that role.

\carmen: @simon that works for me if @security signs off. Can someone open the ticket and create the role? We need it within the 30m change window.

own: I can spin up the role. two notes: 1) security will require MFA-on-session, 2) need to add a condition to the boundary to allow this role by ARN. I'll draft the IAM doc.

aj: FYI — avoid adding global allow to the boundary. Use explicit ARN whitelisting + `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` condition.

maya: Carmen, also confirm we want to pin the release to model-serving:2026-03-18 rather than latest, to avoid accidental config drift.

carmen: yes pinning confirmed. I'll update the release notes and changelog.

simon: I'm going to run the policy simulator against the boundary and the new role (quick check). If it passes I'll merge the role + trust policy.

```bash
# example role trust
aws iam create-role --role-name deployer-releng-temp \
  --assume-role-policy-document file://trust.json
```

ow: please remember to include this in the rollout notes.

oncall-bot: Reminder: change window required for prod deploys between 15:00-16:00 UTC. If escalation needed use #incidents and ping @oncall.

\carmen: thanks everyone. @owen please post the created role ARN here when available and tag security for the exception. If role creation fails we will hold the deploy.

own: created role arn:aws:iam::999999999999:role/deployer-releng-temp and requested security review (ticket DEVSEC-4892). added `aws:MultiFactorAuthPresent` condition.

aj: approved from infra side. will watch the canary and rollback immediately on 5xx spike.

carmen: deploying canary now. will report back in ~5m. :eyes:

deploy-bot: deployment started: canary -> prod (subset). logs: https://deploys.redwood.ai/ops/2378901234

carmen: canary looks clean at 90s. latency within SLO. proceeding with full rollout.

oncall-bot: CHANGE WINDOW: noted. escalation path remains open.

carmen: final: deploy succeeded. closing thread and will attach notes to DEVOPS-1234. thanks for the quick triage. :thumbsup:
